classification.difficultyReason: Convert minutes to hours and model the time saving with reciprocal speeds.

content.prompt: Sally rides to school each morning. She discovers that if she were to ride the 10 km to school at a speed 10 km/h faster than she normally rides, she would get to school 10 minutes earlier. Find Sally’s normal riding speed. (Let $V$ km/h be Sally’s normal speed.)

answer.short:
$20\text{ km/h}$

Compare the journey times in hours.
answer.worked:
Ten minutes is $\frac{1}{6}$ hour. Sally’s usual and faster journey times are $\frac{10}{V}$ hours and $\frac{10}{(V+10)}$ hours, with $V>0$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{10}{V}-\frac{10}{V+10}&=\frac16\\60(V+10)-60V&=V(V+10)\\600&=V^2+10V\\V^2+10V-600&=0\\(V+30)(V-20)&=0\\V&=-30\text{ or }20\end{align*}$$
Reject the negative speed. Sally normally rides at $20\text{ km/h}$. Check: $\frac{10}{20}=\frac{1}{2}$ h and $\frac{10}{30}=\frac{1}{3}$ h, giving a saving of $\frac{1}{6}$ h.
